The nouns change because the sources change them, in both languages: shaban 'mountain' in the summary and 'rise' twice in the body (one Arabic noun); kanzan 'massif', 'a chain of sedimentary and sandy hills' and the 'Mountain' of its name; arbaa 'hills', 'formations', 'a single hill', 'the mountain'; thulaim 'a rocky formation, one of the … hills'. The Urdu follows the English noun for noun. Two things are the Urdu's own and are stated: (1) ruling P3a asks for the common noun «پہاڑ» once in the body of a «جبل» page, so kanzan («اس پہاڑ کا یہی نام») and thulaim («یہ پہاڑ») carry it where the English has a pronoun; (2) the fourth noun he lists, «ساخت», was the Urdu's choice for 'formation' and leaves the text in this round (changes 8, 14, 17 and 19, under his item 5), which takes one noun out of arbaa and one out of thulaim. What he would be driving to — a mountain or a mound — the sources do not settle; logged.

Applied in all four places. «ساخت» is the build of a thing, not a thing one stands in front of: his reading is right, and stage 2 and stage 4 had both called the word stiff and kept it for want of a noun. arbaa: the page's own noun for the four, «ٹیلے» (change 8; the summary and the Russian line say 'hills'). thulaim: «ایک الگ تھلگ چٹان» (change 14; the Russian line says 'a free-standing rock'). tuwaither: «چٹانوں والا» in the summary (change 17) and «ہوا کی تراشی ہوئی چٹانیں» in the body (change 19). His two wordings were «چٹانیں» and «چٹانی ٹیلے». 'Formations' said as 'hills' or 'rocks' is counted under accuracy on the three pages.

«رسوبی» is the source's 'sedimentary' on four pages, in both languages, and the dictionary's word for it; no common Urdu word names the rock (the plain «تہ دار» describes it and says another thing). The register does not outrank the content of the source (the principle of ruling P24). Recorded as the cost it is: a schoolbook word that explains nothing to him, charged in the nativeness of the pages that carry it. That «رسوبی اور ریتلے ٹیلوں» may be one kind of hill or two is the doubt of the English, 'sedimentary and sandy hills'.

The Urdu writes each distance as its own English field writes it: 'some fifteen kilometres' and 'some twenty' in words, 'some 22' in digits, 'about six' and 'about a kilometre' in words. arbaa has digits and words in one paragraph in both languages. Nothing is evened out between pages (the round's rule for figures; the number check holds every English figure in the Urdu). The button's answer is an interface string.

Applied for the town: «الطرف قصبہ» in the body (change 9) and «الطرف قصبے کے قریب» in the card (change 11); item N73 is ruled B, the generic after the name, as the round writes «گاؤں» and «شہر» and as he asks. His misreading shows that the order made it: the generic first, then a word he took for its complement. NOT applied for «محلہ القوع»: «محلہ» before its name is approved text on the pages of round 1 and of b3 and b4 («محلہ الکوت», «محلہ النعاثل», «محلہ المزروعیہ», «محلہ جنوبی الرفعہ») and the wording of rulings N45, N61 and N63; a batch judge does not reopen it. Recorded for whoever may: he is the first reader to say that the place word stands before one kind of name and after the others.

An interface string, final in the interface batch and not edited here. Recorded for the next interface round: «اشتراک کریں» is 'correct but stiff' to this reader, whose phone says the loan (b4's first reader found it bookish, its second natural).
An interface string, final in the interface batch. Recorded for the next interface round with his wording: 'understood at once, slightly odd as a button'; one asks «یہاں سے کتنی دور؟».

Interface strings, final in the interface batch. Recorded for the next interface round: «سیر مکمل کر سکتے ہیں» sounds translated, 'as if my outing were incomplete without them'; the heading above it is brochure language, the fifth reader of the round to say so.

No fault found: the repeated interface strings 'all read naturally'. Recorded for the next interface round, now on a second reader of the round: «یہ مقام محفوظ کریں» can read for half a second as 'protect this place'.

SERIOUS, and the source's, in both languages. The page is filed under the hill near Al-Tuwaither and tells of it only that it is a rocky rise standing apart from Jabal Al-Qarah, where it lies and its two names; every other sentence is about the other mountain (the old name, Yaqut's entry, the caves, the meaning, the palms and waters), and the page ends by sending the reader to that mountain's page. Neither language says what one sees or does here. The Urdu adds nothing and carries nothing over from the jabal-al-qarah page. Logged first among this page's defects; no point is taken from the translation for it.

SERIOUS, and the Urdu's own share of it is cured. In the source the mention is not this hill's: the English ties 'recorded it' by a colon to "'Al-Shaban' was a name of Al-Qarah Mountain itself", and the Arabic's pronoun follows «جبل القارة نفسه» with the headword inside the quotation. The Urdu had cut the sentence in two and left a bare «اس», which spells 'this' and 'that' alike and under this title was read as 'this hill'. Change 2 says the pronoun's two referents, both from the sentence before: «اسی نام سے جبل القارہ کا ذکر». Form, not content (ruling P23); the literal wording is on record. The source's own weakness — a page titled Al-Shab'an that quotes an entry on Al-Shab'an about another mountain — is logged.

Applied in the closing sentence, where the misreading can do harm: the mountain is named where its caves are spoken of, and the page is 'that same famous mountain's' (change 3; the same words, turned round). The cause was the Urdu's: the English keeps 'that famous mountain' apart from 'this neighbouring rise', and unvocalised Urdu writes both «اس». The first «اس مشہور پہاڑ» is left: its clause names the mountain («“القارہ” کا نام»), a circular sentence would come of putting the key there, and since change 2 the paragraph has already said which mountain it is about. No vowel sign is added to tell the two demonstratives apart (ruling P17).

'The historic eastern coastlands' is the English's own bracket, set inside the quotation, and it does not say of which land; the Arabic has no gloss at all. The Urdu says what the bracket says and no more (item N71: the gloss as a sentence of the page's own after the quotation). He understood what the sentence is for. 'Of the Arabian Peninsula' is in neither source and is not supplied; logged for the owner.

Both remarks are the source's. 'Encircled it': the English pronoun does not say which mountain (stage 4 logged it; the German and Russian lines name Jabal Al-Qarah); the Urdu keeps the pronoun, and since change 2 the nearest mountain named before it is Jabal Al-Qarah, which is the one meant. The step from palms and waters to 'the sated one' is left to the reader by the English; the Arabic makes it with a verb ('until it was sated'), which is Arabic-only and is not imported.

«شکم سیر» is the dictionary's word for 'sated' and stands once, in the sentence that gives the meaning of an old name; he says himself that it is 'fine in a history note'. The colloquial «پیٹ بھرا» would be the wrong register for a gloss, and «سیر» alone is spelled like the page's word for a visit. Taste; recorded.

Applied: the second name stands in quotation marks at both mentions, summary (change 0) and body (change 1), as both sources and the three earlier lines have it; item N72 is ruled B. That answers what he says of the summary ('nothing marks it as a name; the quotation marks given to «“الشبعان”» are not given to it'). How the name is said he still cannot tell: no source vowels it or says what it means, and no sign and no gloss is added (ruling P17).

«… کا ہو کر رہ گیا» is Urdu's own idiom for a name that stays with something for good, set by stage 2 in place of an office phrase; he lost the thread 'for a moment' (minor). His wording, «… کے حصے میں آ گیا», is good Urdu too and is on record; the sentence is not rewritten for a moment's pause, and its cost is charged under nativeness.

The two names are the Arabic's («الشعبة», «الشبعان») and each is built from its Arabic spelling; nothing in the Urdu can be changed. What is missing is the source's: the kanzan page says the massif is 'commonly called Al-Shu'bah Mountain' and neither page tells the reader that this is not the Al-Shab'an of the neighbouring page. Logged for the owner: a word on either page, or a link.

Two things. That the summary puts the massif 'north-east of the oasis' and the body 'on the eastern rim of the northern oasis' is the source's, in both languages; logged. 'The northern oasis' is the source's own term, explained nowhere; stage 4 kept it bare for the first blind reading and named the remedy if the reader took it for another oasis — the name at that mention. Applied: «الاحساء کے شمالی نخلستان کے مشرقی کنارے پر» (change 4; item N75, candidate C). The Russian line's reading, 'the northern part of the oasis', which would make one picture of the two, turns the source's term into a description and is on record for the owner.

Neither language says who fought whom or how it ended; both say that the Battle of Kanzan was fought 'in the Kanzan area' («وفي منطقة كنزان وقعت … معركة كنزان»). The Urdu carries the date, the reign, the place and the losses as the source has them and adds no party and no outcome (the reference article names them; not imported). The order of the sentence is stage 1's and stage 2's: any other sets «کنزان کے علاقے میں» against «کنزان کی … لڑائی»; its three asides are charged under nativeness.

Applied for the switch, which was the Urdu's: «بادشاہ» becomes «شاہ», the key's own word, so that the King of the second sentence is the «شاہ عبد العزیز» of the first (change 5); the English has 'King … the King'. NOT applied for the first half: «شاہ عبد العزیز» is a termbase key of round 1, in the applied baiah page and in b4's locked uqair-mosque, and is not reopened; and neither source says 'of Saudi Arabia' or 'the founder', so no marker is supplied. Recorded for the owner and for the entry: to a reader from the subcontinent the name is first the Delhi scholar's.

Applied: «جاں بحق ہوئے» (change 6; item N78). Stage 4 chose «مارے گئے» as neutral and unmistakable against the idiom «کام آئے»; the reader hears it as the word for the enemy's dead. His word is respectful, says that the prince died, and makes no claim of martyrdom, so the Urdu stays with the English ('fell') and does not go over to the Arabic's 'was martyred', which remains the owner's option.

He calls the sentence 'good, natural Urdu'. That the page speaks of a massif and a chain of hills before it says there is soft sand to drive on is the order of the source in both languages; the Urdu keeps it. Recorded with his item 4.

Both languages: 'Al-Ahsa Municipality is developing a major recreational park on the massif', present tense, with no name, date or opening, beside a card that says open public site, round the clock, free. Neither says whether works close any part of the place. The Urdu says 'is building' and states nothing more. Logged with the resort contract of tuwaither, the same defect in a stronger form.
No vowel sign is added to a name and no Latin gloss for its pronunciation (ruling P17); no source vowels «الجرن». Recorded in the two entries: this reader cannot tell how either is said.

Applied: «سلویٰ» (change 7). The Arabic ends in alif maqsura; Urdu writes that ending «یٰ», and without the mark the word reads with a final 'i'. The line had no rule for it: its one precedent, «جمادی الاول», is the Urdu name of a month with its own reference title, not a transliterated place. Ruled as N82; the mark is the letter's Urdu spelling, no vowel sign in the sense of ruling P17, is rejected by no guard and lies inside the font subset's declared range. That nothing says what Salwa is (a town on the road to Qatar) is the source's.

SERIOUS, two halves. The Urdu's: «سڑک کو لوگوں کے لیے سازگار بنانا» is not Urdu to him. Item N79 is decided on this: «لوگوں کے لیے بہتر بنانے» (change 10) — the verb Urdu uses of a road, with the one thing the planning term says, for whom. The literal «انسان دوست» stays on record and is not taken (of a road it reads as a mistranslation, stage 2). The source's: 'to humanise the road' is jargon neither language explains, and the page that most invites a family says nothing of how one reaches the hills today or in what car, while its last sentence implies that reaching them is not yet easy. Nothing of that is supplied; logged high among the defects.

The owner's rule (ruling P16): no English loan where a common Urdu word exists, and a blind reader's preference does not open the door to one. «خیمہ زنی» is the dictionary's word and he understood it. Recorded: formal to him, in summary and body; the Arabic source itself borrows the English word for hiking and the Urdu does not copy that either.

The superlative with its 'one of' is the source's in both languages ('one of southern Al-Ahsa's best-known spots', «من أشهر وجهات»), and a claim worded so follows the Arabic (ruling P19); the frame «… ترین … میں سے ایک» is the approved one of round 1. He calls it common. The three possessives are charged under nativeness.

No fault found: 'this page reads best of the five'. «مخروطی» is the source's 'conical' and he knows it. Recorded: of the two sentences he praises, the first is unchanged, and the sentence between them now says «ٹیلے» for his «ساختیں» (change 8).

Applied in both places: «الاحساء میں داخلے کے شمالی راستے پر» in the summary (change 12) and at the opening of the body (change 13). His misreading is a real one — «داخلی» is first 'internal' — although the reference site does write the phrase for an entrance («داخلی راستہ» 136 pages, «داخلی راستے» 185, among them a city's: «بغداد کے جنوب مشرقی داخلی راستے»; read by the judge on 2026-10-13), so stage 1's wording was not an invention. «داخلے کا راستہ» is the plain Urdu for a way in; as a whole phrase «داخلے کے راستے» has no page on that site, and the wording rests on his misreading and on the judge's own Urdu, not on a count — the next reader is its test. His own wording, «شمال سے داخل ہونے والے راستے پر», would stack two participles in the summary («… ہونے والے راستے پر پڑنے والا»). The word stays an entrance, apart from the 'gate' of the proposals.

Both summaries say only 'the first of Al-Ahsa's landmarks at its northern gateway, just west of Al-Oyoun city' — a landmark, not what kind; and both bodies then say twice more that it is the first thing met from the north. The Urdu carries each as it stands: «مقام» is the source's 'landmark', and a noun for what the place is would be a word from another field. Logged.

Applied: «یہ العیون کے قریب اور نخلستان کی شمالی سڑک کے کنارے ہے» (change 15). The sources are clear that it lies beside two things, the town and the oasis's northern road; the Urdu's one postposition after a possessive chain could be read two ways and he could not settle it after two readings. Each thing has its own postposition now; nothing is added.

Applied (change 16). The circle is the English's ('proposals … remain at the proposal stage') and not the Arabic's ('proposals … still within the frame of ideas'): the closing clause now follows the Arabic's wording, «مگر یہ ابھی خیالات ہی ہیں», as the Russian line does. «ترقی دے کر», which he calls office Urdu of a hill, is dropped: «بنایا جائے» already says what is to become of it. NOT applied: «شمالی سیاحتی دروازہ» is the source's phrase in both languages ('a northern tourist gateway for Al-Ahsa') and stays; that the sentence gives a visitor nothing to act on is the source's, which says itself that these are only ideas.

Missing in both languages: how big the hill is, whether one climbs it, what one sees. The page says where it stands, what kind of hill it is, that it is easy to reach, and that there are proposals. Nothing is supplied.
No vowel sign is added to a name (ruling P17) and no source vowels it. Recorded in the entry: he cannot tell how «الثلیم» is said.

Applied for what is the Urdu's: the opening now sets the place first and the name before its verb, «التویثیر گاؤں کے شمال میں، محلہ القوع میں، جبل ابو حصیص کھڑا ہے۔» (change 18) — ruling N64's other remedy, the build of three other openings of the batch and the order of both sources; the comma after the subject is gone. NOT changed: «محلہ القوع». Both sources put the mountain 'in the Al-Qou' quarter north of Al-Tuwaither village' («في حي القوع شمالي قرية التويثير»), and the round's one word for that Arabic generic is «محلہ» (approved pages; rulings N45, N61, N63). That a quarter holds a mountain, and how the quarter stands to the village, the source does not say; logged, and his picture of a town lane is charged under fit.

The source's, in both languages: the area line says 'Al-Tuwaither village — the eastern villages, Al-Ahsa' while the body puts the mountain in a quarter north of that village; and this one line of the five names a larger place bare, so ruling P20 leads with it, while the other four give two positions and keep the source's order (ruling N30). The Urdu line is the approved build of both tahimiyah lines with the village changed. Logged with the area rows.

Missing in both languages: whether one can go into the grottoes or only feel the air at their mouths, and anything on safety. The Urdu makes no claim either way ('famed for its narrow grottoes, from which cool draughts flow year-round'). Nothing is supplied.

He guessed what is meant, and guessed right. The English hangs 'a trait of Al-Ahsa's sedimentary hills' on a dash after the clause about the cool draughts, the Arabic likewise ('as is the way of …'); a noun in place of «یہ» would decide more than either source does. Kept; the pause is charged under nativeness.

Three things. (1) The register: the source's last sentence is a press notice in both languages ('signed an investment contract to develop and operate the mountain as a tourist resort with eco-friendly rural lodges'), and the Urdu says each of its terms with the plain Urdu equivalent; nothing is softened or cut. The share of the stiffness that is the Urdu's is charged under nativeness. (2) The contract against the card (open, free, round the clock) is the source's, logged first among the defects. (3) THE FIGURE: he converted «100,000» to a lakh in his head. That is item N66, ruled in this file: the line's form for a figure of one lakh is the Urdu scale, «1 لاکھ مربع میٹر». IT IS NOT IN THE TEXT: the stage checker compares by value only a source figure followed by million / M and reports the scaled form of a bare '100,000' as two findings, and a judge does not edit a checker. The digits stand by that limit alone and the decision goes to the coordinator.
No vowel sign is added to a name (ruling P17) and no source vowels either. Recorded in the two entries: he cannot tell how «حصیص» or «القوع» is said.
'Apart from «ساختیں» this reads well': the word is replaced, «ہوا کی تراشی ہوئی چٹانیں» (change 19, with his item 5). The rest of the sentence, which he finds useful, is unchanged.

source_defects.where: tuwaither: body against the card; kanzan: body against the card (reader items 45, 28)
source_defects.defect: tuwaither, both languages: in 2024 the municipality 'signed an investment contract to develop and operate the mountain as a tourist resort with eco-friendly rural lodges over an area of 100,000 square metres', while the card says 'Open public site — no entry fee', 'Open 24 hours', 'Free entry'. Neither language says whether work has begun, whether the hill is still freely open, or whether there will be a charge. kanzan, both languages: the municipality 'is developing a major recreational park on the massif', present tense, no name, date or opening, beside the same three rows.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: Each statement is carried at its strength: the contract is signed and the resort is only its purpose; the park is being built. Nothing passes from the body into the card or back. HARM, the greatest in the batch: 'I would half-trust the card after this sentence' — a family may drive out on a card that the page's own text suggests is out of date. FOR THE OWNER: one line on each page saying what the public may enter today.

source_defects.where: all five pages: the card and the page as a guide (reader items 3, 12, 31, 39, 43)
source_defects.defect: No page says whether an ordinary car reaches the place, whether there is parking, shade, water or a toilet, which season or time of day suits a visit, or how long the road is; none has a bestTime, a 'Good for' row or a FAQ. arbaa invites camping, desert trips and hiking and closes on a road project 'making the landmark easier to reach', which implies that it is not easy now, with no word on how one gets there today. thulaim and tuwaither do not say what one sees or does at the hill, or whether the grottoes can be entered.

source_defects.where: shaban: the whole body (reader items 14 serious, 15 serious, 16, 18)
source_defects.defect: The page is titled for the hill near Al-Tuwaither and is almost wholly about Jabal Al-Qarah: the old name, Yaqut's entry, the caves, the meaning of the name, the palms and waters, and a closing sentence that sends the reader to the other page. Of its own hill it gives the rock, the place and two names. It quotes an entry headed Al-Shab'an, about another mountain, under a title that is Al-Shab'an. Its pronouns do not say which mountain: 'recorded it', 'encircled it', 'that famous mountain', 'the famous mountain'.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: Carried as it is; nothing is brought from the jabal-al-qarah page. MENDED IN FORM under ruling P23, each logged with its literal wording: Yaqut's 'it' is said as 'Jabal Al-Qarah, under this very name' (change 2); the closing sentence names the mountain where its caves are spoken of (change 3); the summary says which name was Jabal Al-Qarah's (N81). 'Encircled it' keeps its pronoun. HARM: the reader 'finished the page not knowing what the place offers', and half-way through expected caves here.

source_defects.defect: Both languages give the date, the reign and the losses of 'the famous Battle of Kanzan' and never say who fought whom or how it ended; the battle of Kanzan is said to have been fought 'in the Kanzan area'. The King is 'King Abdulaziz' with nothing to say of which country, and the prince has no fuller name. The Arabic says the prince 'was martyred', the English that he 'fell'.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: No party, outcome, country or fuller name is added. The King is «شاہ عبد العزیز», the termbase key, and since this round «شاہ» again in the next sentence (change 5); the prince «جاں بحق ہوئے» (N78). HARM: for a 'famous' battle the reader has a date and casualties and no sides; a reader from the subcontinent first thinks of the Delhi scholar of the same name. FOR THE OWNER: the two sides in one clause; and whether the Arabic's word for the prince's death is the one he wants in every language.

source_defects.where: kanzan: summary against body; 'the northern oasis' (reader item 23)
source_defects.defect: The summary puts the massif 'north-east of the oasis'; the body puts it 'on the eastern rim of the northern oasis' and north-east of Hofuf. 'The northern oasis' is used as a known term and explained on no page of the site. The oasis is named in neither field of the source.

The reader could not make one picture of the two. On record for the owner, the Russian line's reading: «نخلستان کے شمالی حصے کے مشرقی کنارے پر».

source_defects.where: tuwaither: area line against body; the quarter; file name (reader items 41, 42)
source_defects.defect: The area line names 'Al-Tuwaither village — the eastern villages, Al-Ahsa'; the body puts the mountain 'in the Al-Qou' quarter north of Al-Tuwaither village'. source_defects.where: thulaim: area line, summary, the closing sentence (reader items 36, 38)

source_defects.effect_on_urdu: Approved pairs, verbatim; the one new value by item N65. The reader read the card twice looking for what the second and third rows add.

source_defects.defect: shaban: 'mountain', then 'rise' twice, for one Arabic noun. kanzan: 'massif', 'a chain of sedimentary and sandy hills', and 'Mountain' in the name; soft sand and dune driving only in the fourth sentence. arbaa: 'hills', 'formations', 'a single hill', 'the mountain'. thulaim: 'a rocky formation, one of the … hills'. 'Sedimentary' stands on four pages and explains nothing to a lay reader; 'sedimentary and sandy hills' may be one kind or two.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: The English noun is followed each time; «پہاڑ» stands once in each body by ruling P3a; 'formation' is said since this round with the page's own nouns (changes 8, 14, 17, 19). The reader cannot tell whether he would drive to a mountain or to a mound.

source_defects.where: shaban: the gloss of 'Bahrain'; the meaning of the name (reader items 17, 18, 19)
source_defects.defect: English only: an editorial gloss set inside Yaqut's quotation, '[the historic eastern coastlands]', which does not say of which land; the Arabic leaves the historical sense of the name unexplained. The English gives the name's meaning as an aside and leaves the step from palms and waters to 'the sated one' unmade; the Arabic makes it with a verb.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: The gloss stands after the quotation as a sentence of the page's own, with the bracket's content and no more (N71; the literal form on record). The meaning is said in a sentence (N70). The reader asks 'eastern coast of what?'.

source_defects.where: kanzan and shaban: two names that look alike (reader item 22); kanzan: the title
source_defects.defect: The kanzan page says the massif is 'commonly called Al-Shu'bah Mountain' («جبل الشعبة»); the neighbouring page is titled Al-Shab'an («جبل الشبعان»). Neither tells the reader that these are two mountains. The kanzan page is filed under the name of the history books, not under the name it says people use today.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: Each name is built from its Arabic spelling; nothing in the Urdu can tell them apart further. The reader took them for one mountain and went back to check.

source_defects.defect: 'A project to humanise the Jabal Al-Arba road' renders an Arabic planning term word for word, and neither language says what is done to the road or when. The road heads 'towards Salwa and Qatar' with nothing to say what Salwa is. The English summary says 'favourite' where the Arabic says 'famous'; the Arabic writes the English word for hiking.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: 'To make the road better for people' (N79); no detail of the works is added. «سلویٰ» stands bare, as its source has it. The evaluative word follows the English (ruling P19).

source_defects.defect: Some distances are words and others digits, within one paragraph on arbaa ('some 22 kilometres', 'about six kilometres'), in both languages; thulaim and shaban give no distance from Hofuf. kanzan puts its massif some fifteen kilometres north-east of Hofuf beside a village that the jalaniyah page puts some twelve away; tuwaither is some twenty kilometres east of Hofuf where tahimiyah-e, in the same belt, is some twelve. No page gives a road distance.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: Each figure as its own field writes it; nothing is converted, completed or evened out.

source_defects.where: tuwaither: the closing sentence; the trait of the hills (reader items 44, 45)
source_defects.defect: The last sentence is a press notice in both languages. 'A trait of Al-Ahsa's sedimentary hills' hangs on a dash and does not say what the trait is — the grottoes, the cool air or the hill. The page says the air is cool all year; the jabal-al-qarah page says its caves are cool in summer and warm in winter, of hills this page calls alike. The English writes the area in digits, the Arabic in words.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: Carried term for term; no season and no time of day is added (C16 untouched). The figure is the source's value in the source's digits (N66).

source_defects.where: remarks on ruled forms and on the interface, recorded for the owner and for the next interface round (reader items 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 25, 29, 32, 40, 46)
source_defects.defect: Not defects of the source. (1) «شاہ عبد العزیز», the termbase key: to a reader from the subcontinent first the Delhi scholar. (2) «محلہ» stands before its name where «گاؤں», «شہر» and now «قصبہ» stand after theirs. (3) Seven names he cannot say aloud: «ابا الکباری», «کنزان», «الجرن», «الثلیم», «حصیص», «القوع», and «سلوی» before its mark. (4) «خیمہ زنی» where he says the loan. (5) Interface: the share button stiff; the distance button 'slightly odd'; the line under the nearby strip 'sounds translated' and its heading brochure language; the save button for half a second 'protect this place'.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: Unchanged: (1) a key of round 1; (2) approved text and rulings N45, N61, N63; (3) ruling P17, no vowel sign — «سلویٰ» alone gains the mark that is its Urdu spelling (N82); (4) ruling P16; (5) the interface batch is final and its strings are not edited here.

source_defects.defect: 'Oyoun' here and 'Uyun' in 'the Uyunid state' on jalaniyah for one Arabic word; 'North-east' and 'Northeast', 'South-east' and 'Southeast' within one page; 'al-Hamawi' in lower case beside 'Al-' in every place name.

changes.before: یاقوت الحموی نے اس کا ذکر یوں کیا ہے
changes.after: یاقوت الحموی نے اسی نام سے جبل القارہ کا ذکر یوں کیا ہے
changes.why: Reader item 15 (serious): he took «اس کا ذکر» for the hill of the page and expected caves here. WHOSE MENTION IT IS IN THE SOURCE: the old Al-Shab'an's, that is Jabal Al-Qarah's. English: "'Al-Shaban' was a name of Al-Qarah Mountain itself: the geographer Yaqut al-Hamawi recorded it as 'a mountain in Bahrain …'" — one sentence, the colon tying 'it' to the name just said to be Jabal Al-Qarah's. Arabic: «فكان «الشبعان» اسماً لجبل القارة نفسه؛ ذكره ياقوت الحموي بقوله: «الشبعان: جبلٌ بالبحرين…»» — the pronoun follows 'Jabal Al-Qarah itself' and the quotation opens with the headword. In neither language is it the hill of the page. The Urdu had made a sentence of its own with a bare «اس», which in Urdu spells 'this' and 'that' alike and, under a page titled with the same name, was read as 'this hill': the doubt was the Urdu's, wider than the source's. Cured by saying the pronoun's two referents, both of which stand in the sentence before: 'under this very name' (the Arabic's headword) and the mountain by its key. No fact enters: that Al-Shab'an was Jabal Al-Qarah's name is the preceding sentence. A change of form (ruling P23), logged; literal wording on record: «یاقوت الحموی نے اس کا ذکر یوں کیا ہے». The key «جبل القارہ» stands whole (C46).

changes.before: اس مشہور پہاڑ کے غاروں اور سیر کی تفصیلات کے لیے جبل القارہ کا صفحہ دیکھیں۔
changes.after: جبل القارہ کے غاروں اور سیر کی تفصیلات کے لیے اسی مشہور پہاڑ کا صفحہ دیکھیں۔

The English keeps 'that famous mountain' apart from 'this neighbouring rise'; unvocalised Urdu writes both demonstratives «اس», so the distinction of the source was lost in the Urdu. In the closing sentence the name and the description change places: the caves and the visit are said of the mountain by its name, and the page is 'that same famous mountain's'. The same words, one letter added («اس» to «اسی»); 'famous', the name and the instruction all stand; no word of the source is dropped. The first «اس مشہور پہاڑ» of the paragraph is left: its own clause names the mountain («“القارہ” کا نام»), and since change 2 the paragraph has named Jabal Al-Qarah four sentences earlier.

changes.before: شمالی نخلستان کے مشرقی کنارے پر
changes.after: الاحساء کے شمالی نخلستان کے مشرقی کنارے پر

That the summary and the body place the massif in different terms (north-east of the oasis; on the eastern rim of the northern oasis) is the source's, in both languages, and is logged.

changes.before: اس میں بادشاہ زخمی ہوئے
changes.after: اس میں شاہ زخمی ہوئے

The switch was the Urdu's: the English says 'King Abdulaziz … the King', one word. The termbase key's own word is repeated. Honorific plural as before. (His other remark, that the key reads first as the Delhi scholar of that name, is on a termbase key and on a source that does not say which king: recorded, not applied.)

changes.before: شہزادہ سعد مارے گئے
changes.after: شہزادہ سعد جاں بحق ہوئے
changes.why: Reader item 26 (minor): «مارے گئے» is 'blunt for a prince of a Muslim royal house on a tourism page; it is the wording used for the enemy's dead'; he expected «جاں بحق ہوئے». English 'fell', Arabic 'was martyred' («استشهد»): the English word is itself the dignified one, and stage 4's «مارے گئے», chosen as neutral and unmistakable against the idiom of stages 1 to 3, is plainer than either source. «جاں بحق ہوئے» is the Urdu press's respectful word for a death (ur.wikipedia, exact phrase, read by the judge on 2026-10-13: 114 pages; «جنگ میں جاں بحق» 2), says that he died and makes no claim of martyrdom, so it does not go over to the Arabic's word. No fact changes. Ruled as N78, with stage 4's wording and the Arabic's on record.

changes.before: سلوی اور قطر
changes.after: سلویٰ اور قطر
changes.why: Reader item 30 (moderate): without its ending mark the name 'reads as salvi, or as the woman's name', and he could not match it to a road sign; '«سلویٰ» is how the word is written in Urdu'. The Arabic ends in alif maqsura («سلوى»), which the letterform guard rejects (U+0649); the Urdu spelling of that ending is «ی» with the superscript alif (U+0670), as in «موسیٰ», «عیسیٰ» and the common noun «سلویٰ». The mark is part of the letter's Urdu spelling, not a vowel sign added for pronunciation (ruling P17 speaks of those, for a name ending in ta marbuta). U+0670 is rejected by no guard (the build's forbidden letters are eight Arabic letterforms, its two izafat signs U+0650 and U+06C2) and lies inside the declared range of the Nastaliq subset (U+0600-06FF). Ruled as N82; the key «سلوی» is retired for «سلویٰ».

changes.before: رسوبی چٹان کی چار مخروطی ساختیں ہیں جو ساتھ ساتھ کھڑی ہیں
changes.after: رسوبی چٹان کے چار مخروطی ٹیلے ہیں جو ساتھ ساتھ کھڑے ہیں
changes.why: Reader item 5 (moderate): «ساخت» is 'the make-up or build of a thing, not a thing you can stand in front of'; «چار مخروطی ساختیں … جو ساتھ ساتھ کھڑی ہیں» read to him as translated geology, and he offered «چٹانیں» or «چٹانی ٹیلے». The four things are called «چار مخروطی ٹیلے» in this page's own summary ('four adjoining conical hills') and «ٹیلہ» in the next sentence; the Russian line also says 'hills' here. The noun of the summary is used; the possessive and the verb agree with it (masculine plural). Counted under accuracy: the English body says 'formations' where its summary says 'hills'.

changes.before: قصبہ الطرف اس کے شمال میں
changes.after: الطرف قصبہ اس کے شمال میں
changes.why: Reader item 8 (moderate): 'I first read «قصبہ الطرف» as "the town on the side" … and did not see it was a name until the card repeated it'; the pages put the place word after the name for a village and a city («التویثیر گاؤں», «العیون شہر») and before it here. Stage 1 had set the generic before the name to fence the homograph («الطرف» is the Urdu «طرف» with an article); the reader shows that the fence failed and that the order itself made the misreading (generic, then a word read as its complement). The generic for a town goes after the name, as the round writes a village and a city, and as he asked. Ruled as N73, candidate B. «محلہ» before its name is approved text on the pages of round 1 and of b3 and b4 and is not touched.

changes.before: لوگوں کے لیے سازگار بنانے
changes.after: لوگوں کے لیے بہتر بنانے
changes.why: Reader item 31 (serious): «سڑک کو لوگوں کے لیے سازگار بنانا» 'is not something one says in Urdu; I do not know what is being done to the road'. Item N79, decided on this evidence. Arabic «مشروعاً لأنسنة طريق جبل الأربع», English 'a project to humanise the Jabal Al-Arba road': a planning term that neither source explains. The literal «انسان دوست» is said in Urdu of persons and outlooks and reads of a road as a mistranslation (stage 2); «سازگار» is said of surroundings and failed the reader. «بہتر بنانا» is what Urdu says of a road, and «لوگوں کے لیے» keeps the one thing the term says, for whom. What is done to the road, and how one reaches the place today, the source does not say and the Urdu does not either: no surface, pavement, lighting, vehicle or date is added. The project is still only launched.

changes.before: قصبہ الطرف کے قریب
changes.after: الطرف قصبے کے قریب
changes.why: The same town in the card, in the order change 9 gives it (reader item 8; item N73). After its name the generic inflects like any noun: oblique «قصبے» before the postposition, as its entry records. The line keeps the source's order and ends in a postposition (ruling N30).

changes.before: الاحساء کے شمالی داخلی راستے پر
changes.after: الاحساء میں داخلے کے شمالی راستے پر
changes.why: Reader item 35 (moderate): «داخلی» is 'internal / domestic' («داخلی امور», «وزارتِ داخلہ»); he first read 'on Al-Ahsa's northern internal road'. English 'at its northern gateway', Arabic 'at its northern entrance' («عند مدخلها الشمالي»). «داخلے کا راستہ» is the Urdu for a way in; the adjective 'northern' moves to the road. Still an entrance, as the Arabic has it, and not the 'gate' the page's proposals speak of («دروازہ»), so the two Arabic words stay apart. 'First' stays a matter of order on the way in (ruling P19).

changes.before: الاحساء کے شمالی داخلی راستے پر
changes.after: الاحساء میں داخلے کے شمالی راستے پر
changes.why: The same phrase at the opening of the body, for the same reason (reader item 35): one wording in the two fields.

changes.before: ایک الگ تھلگ چٹانی ساخت ہے
changes.after: ایک الگ تھلگ چٹان ہے
changes.why: Reader item 5 (moderate), the word «ساخت» for a rock formation (see change 8). English 'a solitary rocky formation', Arabic «تكوين صخري منفرد»; the Russian line says 'a free-standing rock'. «چٹان» is a thing one can stand in front of: the dictionary entry (rekhtadictionary.com/meaning-of-chattaan, read by the judge on 2026-10-13) gives it as a feminine noun, 'rock, large block of stone, cliff, stony mound or hill' («پہاڑ کا ابھرا یا نکلا ہوا حصہ … پتھریلی زمین، پہاڑ»). The sentence goes on to call it one of the sedimentary desert hills, as the source does.

changes.before: یہ العیون اور نخلستان کی شمالی سڑک کے پہلو میں ہے
changes.after: یہ العیون کے قریب اور نخلستان کی شمالی سڑک کے کنارے ہے
changes.why: Reader item 37 (moderate): 'I could not parse it: beside [Al-Oyoun] and beside [the oasis's northern road], or beside the northern road of [Al-Oyoun and the oasis]? Read twice, still not sure.' The sources are clear: 'beside Al-Oyoun and the northern oasis road', Arabic «بجوار العيون وطريق الواحة الشمالي» — two things it lies beside. The one postposition after a possessive chain made the Urdu's doubt. Each of the two now has its own postposition: near the town, at the side of the road. The road is still the oasis's northern road, as the Arabic has it; the town stays bare, as its source has it here. Nothing is added.

changes.before: کہ اسے ترقی دے کر الاحساء کا شمالی سیاحتی دروازہ بنایا جائے، مگر یہ خیالات ابھی تجویز کے مرحلے ہی میں ہیں۔
changes.after: کہ اسے الاحساء کا شمالی سیاحتی دروازہ بنایا جائے، مگر یہ ابھی خیالات ہی ہیں۔
changes.why: Reader item 38 (moderate): '"They have given proposals … but these ideas are still at the proposal stage" goes in a circle. «اسے ترقی دے کر» is office Urdu for a hill.' The circle is the English's ('proposals have been floated … ideas that remain at the proposal stage'); the Arabic has none: «طُرحت مقترحات أهلية … ما تزال في إطار الأفكار», proposals that are still only ideas. The Urdu follows the Arabic's wording here, as the Russian line does ('but so far it has gone no further than ideas'): both sources carry 'ideas', and nothing is strengthened — still no project, body, plan or date. 'To develop it as a gateway' is said as 'that it be made the gateway': the converb stage 4 set for 'develop' is dropped, because the finite verb already says what is to become of the hill (the batch renders 'develop … as a resort' the same way on tuwaither, «بنا کر»). Counted under accuracy. Literal wordings on record: «اسے ترقی دے کر … بنایا جائے»; «یہ خیالات ابھی تجویز کے مرحلے ہی میں ہیں».

changes.before: چٹانی ساختوں والا
changes.after: چٹانوں والا
changes.why: Reader item 5 (moderate), the word «ساخت» for a rock formation (see changes 8 and 14). English 'A mountain of cool grottoes and rock formations', Arabic «وتشكيلات صخرية». «چٹانوں والا پہاڑ» is a craggy mountain; 'wind-carved' is the body's word and is not brought into the summary. Counted under accuracy: 'formations' is said as 'rocks'.

changes.before: جبل ابو حصیص، التویثیر گاؤں کے شمال میں، محلہ القوع میں کھڑا ہے۔
changes.after: التویثیر گاؤں کے شمال میں، محلہ القوع میں، جبل ابو حصیص کھڑا ہے۔
changes.why: Reader item 41 (moderate): 'the comma straight after the subject is … not Urdu punctuation', and he could not picture a mountain 'north of the village' and 'in a محلہ' at once. Ruling N64 gives two remedies where a page's name would stand against another proper name in the opening and leaves the choice to the judge of the page: a comma after the name, or the place first. The place comes first here, as on kanzan, arbaa and thulaim, and as both sources have it ('In the Al-Qou' quarter north of Al-Tuwaither village … rises Abu Husais Mountain'). The same words; only the subject moves to stand before its verb. That the mountain lies in a quarter («حي»), which the round writes «محلہ», is the source's statement and is logged.

changes.before: ہوا کی تراشی ہوئی چٹانی ساختیں
changes.after: ہوا کی تراشی ہوئی چٹانیں
changes.why: Reader items 5 and 47: apart from «ساختیں» the sentence 'reads well and tells me something useful'. English 'wind-carved rock formations', Arabic «تشكيلاته الصخرية التي نحتتها الرياح»: rocks the wind has carved. Feminine plural, as before («چٹانیں اور … ڈھلانیں … پہچان ہیں»).

calibration.question: The pronouns of the class «جنہیں / انہیں / انہوں / جنہوں / تمہیں»: U+06C1, or U+06BE («جنھیں / انھیں …»)?
candidates: A — U+06C1: «جنہیں», «انہیں», «انہوں», «جنہوں» (the provisional spelling; ruled for these four; in no string of the text since round 2)
B — U+06BE: «جنھیں», «انھیں», «انھوں», «جنھوں»
calibration.evidence: ROUND 2: the entry is rewritten so that it stands alone and says only what was measured. WHERE IT WAS MET: round 1's text of uqair-mosque::summary carried «جنہیں» once, the first pronoun of the class in any Urdu text of the site; two blind readers read it there and neither remarked on its spelling. Since round 2 that clause is worded with «جن کی» (change 0 of b4's round 2, made because two readers rejected the clause's verb, not for the spelling). So no string of b4, of b3 or of the applied site carries a pronoun of the class today: by the judge's script (b4/s7b-pre.mjs), the four forms and their U+06BE spellings occur 0 times in every Urdu value of the 58 attraction files (11 carry Urdu), in src/i18n/ui.ts, in tm.json and in b3's round-2 text. WHAT IS SOUND. (1) Press, by script on 2026-10-13 (b4/s7-p22-press.mjs, output s7-p22-press.out.txt): on the three outlets from which article text was fetched — urdunews.com (the Gulf's Urdu paper), express.pk, independenturdu.com — these pronouns are written with a heh and never with U+06BE: 12 and 0, 15 and 0, 18 and 0 tokens; on bbc.com/urdu with U+06BE and never with a heh: 0 and 44.
